key_insight: Provides the first comprehensive, practitioner-oriented synthesis of explainability methods for protein language models, identifying which XAI techniques map most clearly to biological concepts (structure, function, motifs) and where gaps remain. It distills principles and evaluation criteria to make model explanations more biologically meaningful.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of organized guidance on how to interpret protein language models—clarifying which explainability methods are appropriate for sequence→structure/function claims and highlighting methodological and evaluation gaps that hinder biological trust and utility.
method: Systematic literature survey of explainable AI techniques applied to protein language models, spanning attribution, probing, attention analysis, generative and causal approaches.
Taxonomy and comparative analysis that maps XAI methods to biological questions (e.g., residue importance, motif discovery, long-range interactions) and evaluation desiderata.
Synthesis of best practices, benchmark considerations, and open challenges to guide method selection and future research.
impact: Helps ML practitioners and computational biologists choose and evaluate interpretability tools that produce biologically meaningful insights, improving model trust, debugging, and downstream applications like protein design and functional annotation.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram: tree linking XAI classes (attribution, probing, attention, generative, causal) to the biological questions they address (motifs, contacts, function).
Method vs. criteria heatmap: rows = XAI methods, columns = evaluation criteria (biological validity, robustness, granularity, scalability), with color-coded suitability.
Pipeline schematic: from protein sequence → language model → chosen XAI method → biological interpretation (structure/function) with decision points.
Case-study snapshot: sequence with colored residue attributions mapped onto a 3D protein outline to illustrate how explanations align with known motifs/contacts.
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
